  token. Log user ids, request ids, and outcomes.
- A disabled account is rejected at sign-in with `403 ACCOUNT_DISABLED`, and
  its existing sessions and realtime connections are revoked at once. Do not
  add a parallel "active" flag.

## Verification

- Anonymous requests to a protected route return `401` with the standard error body, `error.reason` `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`; the same request with a session returns the route's own response.
- An authenticated request that lacks permission returns `403` from
  authorization, not `401`.
- A `required` route redirects an anonymous browser to `/login`; a `guest`
  route redirects a signed-in browser to `/`.
- After sign-out the previous cookie no longer authenticates.
- A new sign-in method signs a new user in, signs an already bound user in,
  rejects an invalid, expired, or reused credential, and creates exactly one
  binding under concurrent first sign-ins.
- A migration added for a sign-in method runs `up` and `down` against a real
  test database.
- The application passes `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, and `build`. Skill
  synchronization alone proves only that the copy matches this source.

## Trusted plugin API

`Auth.pluginApi<TPlugin>(pluginId)` returns only the registered plugin’s API methods through Better Auth’s normal dispatch, including before and after hooks. It does not expose the full authentication context and does not authenticate a caller. `Auth.forConnection(connection)` binds those operations to a caller-owned transaction. Consumers still enforce authorization; HTTP-specific hooks must explicitly check for `request` or `headers` instead of accidentally denying trusted server calls.

## Initial administrator

Before the first seed run, set `users.initialAdmin.username`, `users.initialAdmin.email` and `users.initialAdmin.password` in application configuration to customize the bootstrap account. Omitting the entire node preserves `nocobase` / `admin@nocobase.com` / `admin123`; an explicit node requires a nonempty password and defaults the username to `nocobase` and the email to `admin@nocobase.com`. Usernames contain 3–30 letters, digits, underscores or dots, emails must be valid addresses, and both are stored lowercase. Initialization only runs when the user table is empty, hashes the password and grants the newly created account root permission through the authorization plugin. After initialization, configuration changes do not reset accounts or rerun the recorded seeds. The root permission seed selects the administrator by the same configured username. Use the user administration service for subsequent account changes. Do not edit historical seeds or add a competing administrator seed.

## Trusted server session creation

`Auth.signInUser(userId, request, { clientAddress }?)` creates an ordinary browser session for an existing enabled person account after trusted server code has authorized that sign-in. It returns a `Response`; the caller checks its status and forwards its `Set-Cookie` headers. Better Auth applies the configured session hooks and cookie attributes, without reading or changing the password. There is no HTTP endpoint for this method. The calling plugin owns the access policy: Demo Mode uses it only while public quick sign-in is enabled. This method does not grant permissions or replace authentication for ordinary public login routes.

skills.name: nocobase-app-plugin-authorization
skills.desc: Design and implement NocoBase 3 business permissions: job responsibilities, pages, business actions, fields, record scopes, relations, team inheritance, permission assignments, administration and inspection. Use when building a system or feature whose users have different access.
skills.body:
---
name: nocobase-app-plugin-authorization
description: 'Design and implement NocoBase 3 business permissions: job responsibilities, pages, business actions, fields, record scopes, relations, team inheritance, permission assignments, administration and inspection. Use when building a system or feature whose users have different access.'
metadata:
  short-description: Design and develop business authorization
  domain-owner: '@nocobase/app-plugin-authorization'
---

# Authorization development

Use the application's existing authorization service. Resolve `authorizationToken` from `@nocobase/app-plugin-authorization/server` in a provider or route factory. Read the application's `AGENTS.md` and inspect registered plugins and `server/config/authorization.ts` first. Application-owned features stay in the application's providers/routes/services; create a reusable plugin only when requested.

## Identify model and configuration changes

Inspect existing declarations, enforcement, permission sets and installed capability Skills. Classify each requested change by its content, whether the feature is new or already exists. A request can require both model development and configuration.

| Requested change                                                                                                                                      | Work required                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Add or change supported operations, field/relation capabilities, scope resolver logic, inheritance resolution or server enforcement                   | Develop the permission model and its execution path, then configure the affected business permissions |
| Change who holds an existing action, select an existing record-access strategy or its supported parameters, or adjust assignments and supported rules | Update permission configuration through the management HTTP API or authorized services                |
| Existing declarations have the right names but different behavior from the requirement                                                                | Correct the model; matching names alone do not establish that configuration is sufficient             |

For permission development, deliver both the implemented model and usable initial configuration based on the responsibility matrix: permission sets, pages/actions, selected scopes, applicable rules and intended user/team assignments. Do not stop at registration and leave configuration to the user unless they explicitly requested model-only work. If recipient identities or access decisions are missing, ask for those specifics while completing independent work; do not guess assignments. Keep configuration editable in the backend and preserve unrelated administrator choices.

Choose delivery by installation state: use seeds for fresh-install defaults and authorized runtime services or a controlled data-change workflow for an existing installation. These are ways to apply configuration, not alternatives to model development. Reuse current management pages and editors. When the App owns a role editor, build it from the UI Library's `permission-editor` component (`yes n | pnpm exec shadcn add @nocobase/permission-editor`; its example is `@nocobase/permission-editor-demo`), selecting the actual application capabilities that administrators need to configure and composing its sections and rows in application-owned code. Registry provides no fixed business catalog. Preserve actual action names, descriptions and independent data scopes; do not copy a full options response or demo catalog into the form. Do not generate a default System and tools category or expose unused optional rule editors. The controlled checkboxes edit a draft saved by the host form. Read the relevant references as needed, beginning with the business workflow for model changes and the service/configuration references for configuration changes.

Map independently assignable business operations to their actual UI entries, server requests, affected fields and scopes. Keep permission titles aligned with operation labels; do not hide independent approval, rejection or repair steps behind a generic Manage action. A shared operation on multiple pages uses the same permission. The server enforces the operation and scopes separately from lifecycle eligibility. When splitting existing actions, migrate stored grants and default, sharing and restriction rules without widening ranges. See [the client development reference](references/client-development.md#match-permissions-to-real-business-operations) for the Registry composition and verification contract.

## Start from business responsibilities

Before writing grants, turn the requirement into a matrix: actor/job, page, business action, allowed records, readable/writable fields, relation operations and exceptions. Identify who administers assignments separately from who uses the business feature. Ask only about missing decisions that affect access; record concrete assumptions and continue independent modeling work.

Use jobs as permission sets, such as sales engineer or delivery specialist. Ownership, region and assigned projects are record scopes, not extra role names. A person may hold a direct job plus an inherited team job. Define whether revoking one source should preserve the other. Describe each exception as a business fact: a delegated quote, a confidential project, or an active delivery team.

The sales workflow in [the business module workflow](references/business-module.md) separates quote preparation from regional submission responsibility: an engineer can edit their own out-of-region draft but cannot submit it unless the parent project is also accessible. This is a useful model for multi-table operations; copy the responsibility boundary, not its sample ids.

## Choose the implementation reference

| Task                                                                                                               | Read                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Build a feature from model through routes, assignments and verification                                            | [Business module workflow](references/business-module.md)                                                                                                       |
| Declare typed actions, scopes, fields and nested relations                                                         | [Fluent declarations](references/fluent-registration.md)                                                                                                        |
| Bind generated CRUD to business actions or choose a custom business endpoint                                       | [Repository route integration](references/repository-routes.md)                                                                                                 |
| Assign permission sets to departments, positions or another organisation structure                                 | The application development Skill's `references/organization.md`; it builds the organisation first when the application has none                                |
| Design who gets what across departments, department heads and cross-department work                                | The application development Skill's `references/organization/permission-design.md`; the core needs permission sets only                                         |
| Team or department subject registration, default/sharing/restriction design, protected assignments and diagnostics | [Subjects and administration](references/subjects-and-administration.md)                                                                                        |
| Configure a baseline, collaboration exception or exclusion                                                         | Installed sibling `nocobase-app-plugin-authz-default-access`, `nocobase-app-plugin-authz-sharing-rules`, or `nocobase-app-plugin-authz-restriction-rules` Skill |

Read [runtime setup and APIs](references/runtime-api.md) for installation, registration and management endpoints, [client development](references/client-development.md) for routes, buttons and record eligibility, [code versus seeds](references/code-and-seeds.md) before writing installation data, and [request checks and permission-set services](references/core-api.md) for assignments, protection and transaction contracts. The package README at `node_modules/@nocobase/app-plugin-authorization/README.md` is the complete API reference, and `node_modules/@nocobase/authorization/README.md` defines the underlying terms.

This Skill and its bundled references are self-contained: one sales collaboration and delivery domain of projects, quotes and orders runs through them as the worked example. Implement the included patterns in the App's own feature files through public package exports.

Code defines the business permission model; seeds initialize editable business permission configuration. Administrators can subsequently change seeded sets, scopes, rules and assignments in the backend. App features register their own composites and leave platform/system permission configuration to its owning plugins. See [code versus seeds](references/code-and-seeds.md) for the boundary and examples.

Read [optional capability discovery](references/optional-capabilities.md) before using any rule plugin. A missing corresponding Skill means the capability is unsupported in the current App and needs separate development; do not assume its APIs or tables exist.

## Implement in this order

1. Declare schema and relationships through self-contained migrations. Choose stable composite, page and data scope names. Keep authorization decisions out of migration code.
2. Declare reusable collection permissions with `defineDatabasePermission`; compose user-facing business operations as composite resources with `defineCompositeResource` from `@nocobase/authorization/core`. Explicitly name fields, relation capabilities and every collection a workflow touches.
3. In the owning provider's `boot`, opt collections in with `authz.database.collections.add`, register composites with `authz.compositeResources.define`, record access with `authz.recordAccess.define` and settings items with `authz.settings.add`. Then add a workspace subsection with `authz.ui.sections.add({ name, title, parent })` and list each composite or settings item in it with `authz.ui.place(reference, { section, group? })` (this describes available capabilities and their suggested grouping; the application chooses which resources and actions its configuration page exposes. An unplaced composite or settings item goes under its default section's Other in the options catalog with a startup warning, and a misplaced one fails a development start). Pages are not registered on the server: the client route tree lists them. Release subject registrations at shutdown.
4. Protect every server route with authentication. For a simple single-scope Repository operation, keep `defineRepositoryApiRoutes` and add `authz.database.authorizeRepository` to map methods to composite actions; it reuses or initializes the request's authorization context. For workflows, persisted-state checks, multiple data scopes or custom responses, install `authz.middleware()`, call `c.get('authz').authorize()` once and bind every returned collection policy with `repository.withPolicy()`. Follow [Repository route integration](references/repository-routes.md).
5. Declare `authz` on every entry client route (nested pages inherit it; an omitted one defaults to root-only or `'skip'` with a development warning), add `useCan` for action visibility and obtain per-record eligibility from the server when needed. Handle pending and error states without displaying stale access.
6. Complete the accompanying permission configuration from the responsibility matrix: sets, page and action grants, selected data scopes, supported rules and intended assignments. Use seeds for fresh installations and authorized provisioning for existing installations; editing a seed does not update a running App. Resolve optional capabilities through their installed Skills and preserve unrelated administrator edits.
7. Verify denied as well as allowed requests through the production route factory and actual database policies. Then verify the UI with ordinary users and inherited memberships.

## Enforcement rules

- Register collections explicitly with `authz.database.collections.add({ name, title, actions? })`. Metadata comes from the database; registration grants nothing. Unregistered collections are denied even to unrestricted users.
- `settings`, `composite` and `database.collection` are catalog types: a check on an unregistered item or action is denied with `RESOURCE_ACTION_NOT_SUPPORTED`. `page`, `user` and `notification` are record types that declare actions only; their grants use `id: '*'` for every record.
- A composite action composes exactly the grants it lists, never another composite. A data scope targets the one collection its grant actions name, whose type must declare `recordAccess` (`database.collection` does). Grant page access separately; a page grant never authorizes a server endpoint.
- `can` is for feature visibility. `require` needs an unconditional permit and rejects conditional decisions. Business endpoints use `authorize`, reject denial or missing policies, and consume `conditions.database` without resolving collection grants again.
- For simple business CRUD, keep the Repository route definition and bind each method to its composite action with `authz.database.authorizeRepository`. Multi-scope actions and workflow transitions need custom handlers. `authz.database.policyFor` folds collection grants; without its third argument it does not respect a business-action boundary.
- Scope every read and write in the workflow, including parent lookups. Keep multi-record writes transactional and include expected business state in mutation predicates. Authorization does not validate a quote's amount or its workflow transition.
- Fields and relation operations are code-owned. Permission configuration covers pages, business actions, their data scopes and settings items; do not build a raw-field permission editor.
- Relation writes do not inherit the target collection's standalone constraints. Declare target record access and join-table fields explicitly; keep foreign-key fields from bypassing association controls.
- An authorization context caches grants and rules. Reuse one within a request; create a new one for a new request or identity. Do not persist decisions in module state.

## Completion evidence

Report the responsibility matrix implemented, model changes, configuration actually applied or prepared for installation, who can manage assignments, and observed allow/deny outcomes. Distinguish a written seed from one executed successfully; identify any unresolved recipient identities or access decisions. Cover no grant, page-only, action-only, out-of-scope rows, forbidden fields, invalid relation targets, multiple authorization sources and revocation. If optional plugins or required schema are absent, report that concrete limitation; never replace the missing boundary with an unconditional grant.

Permission Set reads return an opaque `revision`. Editors should send it as `expectedRevision` in `PATCH /api/authorization/permissionSets/:key`; the store atomically compares and replaces it in the update transaction. A stale revision returns 409 `PERMISSION_SET_CONFLICT` and leaves stored grants unchanged. Preserve the draft, offer explicit reload, and do not automatically retry. Existing callers may omit the precondition for compatibility. The server API equivalent is `permissionSets.update(key, changes, expectedRevision)`. The additive, reversible `202610150001_authorization_permission_set_revision` migration initializes existing rows without changing their grants.

skills.body:
---
name: nocobase-app-plugin-concurrency
description: Configure and consume NocoBase 3 process-local Mutex locks, strict named managers, original service Token, optional TTL, public implementation extensions and application-owned shutdown.
---

# Concurrency

## Install and register

Install `@nocobase/app-plugin-concurrency` with compatible application-supplied `@nocobase/app-server`, `@nocobase/service-provider` and `@nocobase/concurrency` peers. Register the default `/server` definition before business plugins and register `defineConcurrencyConfig()` from `/config` under `concurrency`. Installation and both registrations are separate requirements.

The factory supplies `default: memory` and `backends.memory.adapter: mutex`, declares `CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT` and exposes no browser fields. Entry fields are `adapter`, optional `namespace` (application name by default), optional `ttl`, and implementation-owned `connection`. Mutex forbids connection. TTL is a renewable lease duration, an integer from 1 through 2147483647 milliseconds. Local Mutex accepts and validates TTL but ignores it, with no holding timer, expiration release or local renewal. Resource TTL overrides configuration TTL; `undefined` retains configuration TTL. Unknown options and invalid selectors fail. Entries do not inherit from one another. Two enabled local entries cannot share a namespace.

## Consume the original service

```ts
import { concurrencyServiceToken } from '@nocobase/app-plugin-concurrency/server';

const service = app.container.resolve(concurrencyServiceToken);
// Obtain managers in ready or normal running work.
const manager = await service.getManager();
const executor = await manager.createSynchronous('orders:sync');
const result = await executor.tryRun(async () => 'done', 500);
```

Inject the owner-created Token; never create a second Token or service. The same configuration name shares one manager. Same-name Lock and Executor handles compete in the same domain regardless of TTL. Use bounded, stable resource names: the local native Mutex table remains until instance shutdown. Local locks coordinate only within that instance, never across processes.

`lock` and `run` wait without a deadline until success, cancellation or failure. Omitted/zero positional try budgets use native `tryAcquire`, including its zero-millisecond timer window. Positive try budgets use native `withTimeout`, not a precise return deadline. Busy results come only from explicit native non-acquisition. Capture each call's signal once; cancellation before delivery must not affect other waiters. Cancellation after delivery does not release a Lease or stop a runner. Late native success after cancellation is released using its own releaser without delivery, runner execution or TTL timer.

Lease release is asynchronous and idempotent; concurrent calls share a result and failures permit explicit retry on the same handle while its instance remains usable. Executors combine Lock acquisition with a no-argument runner, wait for actual runner settlement and diagnose cleanup failure without replacing business values or exceptions. Local Mutex remains held beyond an explicit TTL until manual release, actual runner settlement or instance shutdown. TTL is not a runner timeout or a validity guarantee. Redis implementations use native automatic renewal for both Lock and Executor, not an Executor-owned renewal loop. Use application transactions and idempotency where required.

The Provider owns initialization and shutdown. Default startup is eager; named configurations initialize lazily and concurrently share one initialization. Boot freezes the complete snapshot, including unused entries. Reload requires restart to apply changes and never changes active or lazy domains.

Applications stop dependent business work before Concurrency shutdown. skills.name: nocobase-app-plugin-database-explorer
skills.desc: Browse an application's database connections, collections, and fields read-only through the Database Explorer endpoints, and grant access to them.
skills.body:
---
name: nocobase-app-plugin-database-explorer
description: Browse an application's database connections, collections, and fields read-only through the Database Explorer endpoints, and grant access to them.
---

# Database Explorer

## Use this Skill when

Someone needs to see what databases an application talks to, which collections live on each one, or what fields and physical columns a collection has — and when a role other than System Administrator should be able to see that.

It is not for changing anything. The plugin has no write endpoint, and creating or altering a collection belongs to migrations.

## Public surfaces

Four read endpoints:

| Method and path                                                                            | Returns                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /api/databaseExplorer/connections`                                                    | Every configured connection; the default one has `isDefault: true`            |
| `GET /api/databaseExplorer/connections/:connection/collections`                            | One page of collections; `pageSize` is 1–100 (default 20), `pageToken` opaque |
| `GET /api/databaseExplorer/connections/:connection/collections/:collection`                | The resolved definition, its fields, and resolution warnings                  |
| `GET /api/databaseExplorer/connections/:connection/collections/:collection/physicalSchema` | Physical columns, indexes, keys, and constraints                              |

Success is `{ data }`; the connection list is `{ data, meta: { total } }` and the collection list `{ data, meta: { nextPageToken? } }`. Failures use the standard `/api` error body with `domain` `databaseExplorer`; branch on `reason`: `DATABASE_EXPLORER_FORBIDDEN` (403), `CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND` and `COLLECTION_NOT_FOUND` (404), `INVALID_CURSOR` and `INVALID_LIST_OPTIONS` (400), and `DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE`, `CONNECTION_UNAVAILABLE`, `CONNECTION_UNREACHABLE` and `SCHEMA_READ_DENIED` (503). A malformed `pageSize` or `pageToken` is `400 INVALID_INPUT` in the `app` domain.

The running application documents these routes under the `DatabaseExplorer` tag at `/api/swagger/docs` (JSON at `/api/swagger`, signed in); their operationIds are `databaseExplorerListConnections`, `databaseExplorerListCollections`, `databaseExplorerGetCollection` and `databaseExplorerGetPhysicalSchema`.

The client entry exports `DatabaseExplorerClient`, a typed client for these endpoints, and `DATABASE_EXPLORER_ACCESS`, the grant they check. The plugin contributes no pages; an application that wants one builds it on the client and declares it among its own routes with that grant. The server entry also exports the read functions (`listConnections`, `listCollections`, `readCollection`, `readPhysicalCollection`), the `DATABASE_EXPLORER_PAGE` constant, and the response types.

## Prerequisites

Register `@nocobase/app-plugin-authentication` and `@nocobase/app-plugin-authorization` before this plugin on both runtimes. An application configured with `database.default: none` gets `503 DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE` from every endpoint.

## App workflow

Add the plugin to both composition roots and to the application's `dependencies`:

```ts
// server/plugins.ts
import databaseExplorer from '@nocobase/app-plugin-database-explorer/server';

// client/plugins.ts
import databaseExplorer from '@nocobase/app-plugin-database-explorer/client';
// then call it: databaseExplorer()
```

A System Administrator can already read the endpoints, because that permission set grants `page:*/access`. To let another role in, add one grant to its permission set:

```json
{
  "resource": { "type": "page", "id": "database-explorer" },
  "actions": [{ "action": "access" }]
}
```

An application page built on the endpoints declares its route with the same grant (`DATABASE_EXPLORER_ACCESS`), so the navigation entry and the endpoints never disagree.

## Ownership

The plugin owns the access resource, its endpoints and their response shapes, and the rule about what a connection may reveal. Applications own whether the plugin is registered, any page built on it, and who is granted access.

Connection responses never carry a password, user name, host, port, socket path, SQLite filename, TLS material, driver options, or pool settings. That list is enforced as an allow-list in `server/connection-summary.ts`, so a field a new dialect adds stays inside by default. Do not turn it into a deny-list, and do not add a locator to it because a screen looks sparse. The same restraint applies to logs: a driver error is recorded by classification only, never by message or cause.

The Explorer issues no writes of its own. On a managed connection, a first collection read can initialize `__nocobase_collection_metadata`, its companion cache-version table, and the initial version row, including bookkeeping added by an upgrade. Business collections, their rows, and existing metadata documents remain unchanged; subsequent reads also leave all bookkeeping rows unchanged. External connections use a directory-backed metadata store and do not create these tables.

skills.name: nocobase-app-plugin-demo-mode
skills.desc: Build, enable or operate a dedicated NocoBase 3 demo deployment with @nocobase/app-plugin-demo-mode: a public, shared demo site whose fictional data is generated, cleared and reset, with quick visitor sign-in, write protection and optional model or Agent simulation (公开演示站、只读演示、定时重置的演示环境、 Demo Mode). Also use when changing business collections, external integrations or background jobs in an application that already depends on this plugin, so its demo dataset, cleanup and adapters stay complete. Not for example records (use the application development Skill's sample-data workflow), ordinary trial, staging or customer deployments, third-party sandbox credentials, or an in-app presentation/display mode feature.
skills.body:
---
name: nocobase-app-plugin-demo-mode
description: >-
  Build, enable or operate a dedicated NocoBase 3 demo deployment with
  @nocobase/app-plugin-demo-mode: a public, shared demo site whose fictional data
  is generated, cleared and reset, with quick visitor sign-in, write protection
  and optional model or Agent simulation (公开演示站、只读演示、定时重置的演示环境、
  Demo Mode). Also use when changing business collections, external integrations
  or background jobs in an application that already depends on this plugin, so
  its demo dataset, cleanup and adapters stay complete. Not for example records
  (use the application development Skill's sample-data workflow), ordinary trial,
  staging or customer deployments, third-party sandbox credentials, or an in-app
  presentation/display mode feature.
---

# Demo Mode

Use `@nocobase/app-plugin-demo-mode` for a dedicated demo with its own database and storage. The plugin supplies data lifecycle, visitor accounts, write protection, management components and optional simulation. The application supplies its business records, cleanup and external adapters. Simulation adapters and demo chat are enabled by default once integrated, without AI switches on the management page; the application chooses which flows to connect.

## Check that this Skill applies

Demo Mode refuses ordinary writes, resets data daily and deletes all business data on clear/reset. Apply it only when the user asks for a demo deployment with those properties, names this plugin or Demo Mode, or the application already depends on it. Otherwise use the matching workflow:

| Request                                                                                | Use instead                                                        |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Example or sample records, such as “add some demo customers”                           | The application development Skill's sample-data workflow           |
| A trial, staging, test or customer environment where users keep their own data         | The `nocobase-deployment` Skill; an ordinary deployment without it |
| A payment, mail or other provider's sandbox account or test credentials                | That integration's configuration                                   |
| An in-app “demo/presentation mode” feature, such as hiding fields while screen-sharing | Ordinary feature development                                       |

When the request could mean either a Demo Mode deployment or one of these, ask which one the user wants before registering the plugin, enabling it or adding full-business cleanup. For a confirmed dedicated demo, reuse the user's established deployment, language and role choices, and clarify any unresolved deployment or cleanup scope: clear/reset removes all business data in the demo instance, including visitor additions.

## Keep protection proportionate

A demo is a public showcase: anyone may enter any listed account, administrators included, and the fictional data is reset daily. Protect only what lies outside the demo: a dedicated database and storage, no real credentials or customer data, and no real external effects such as mail, payments, publishing or real models. Inside the demo, use the application's existing permissions as they are and the plugin's defaults. Do not add hardening such as ownership rechecks, rate limits, confirmation steps, management restrictions for dataset accounts or security-focused tests unless the user asks; prefer the simplest integration that shows the requested journeys.

## Integration workflow

1. **Confirm the target and enable.** Check [the dedicated deployment](#confirm-the-dedicated-deployment), then complete [enable the deployment](#enable-the-deployment) and its verification. Check the required host capabilities below.
2. **Provide the dataset.** Adapt the application's business services using [data adaptation](references/adapting-data.md). For a new application with no business domain, use the [executable non-AI example](references/minimal-example.md). Register one dataset on the original `demoDataToken` in an application provider's `boot()`; registration does not generate records.
3. **Adapt interactions.** Keep normal business authorization. Enable [collection write exceptions](references/policies.md#collection-write-exceptions) for visitor mutations. The guard covers request-scoped database writes; adapt [external calls and background work](references/integration-checklist.md) where the application has them. Read [simulation](references/simulation.md) only for AI or Runner flows the demo uses.
4. **Provide entry and management.** Mount `DemoModeSettings` from `@nocobase/app-plugin-demo-mode/client/settings` on an application-owned page inside the application's existing System management (settings) navigation group, protected by `settings:demoMode.data/read`. Wrap its route declarations with `demoModeRoutes([...])` from `@nocobase/app-plugin-demo-mode/client` so both the menu and route are absent outside Demo Mode, including for root. `defineDemoModeConfig()` publishes the enabled flag automatically; existing applications must adopt the helper. Grant [management access](#management-access) and see the [route example](references/minimal-example.md#2-wire-existing-composition-roots). Visitor accounts keep their business permissions. The Client plugin automatically enters Super Admin for anonymous visitors opening the home page or a protected application route and provides `/demo-sign-in` for all enabled person accounts; mount the standalone `DemoModeMenu` in the top header actions as described in [visitor entry](references/visitor-entry.md#required-header-entry).
5. **Generate and verify.** Generate through the [CLI or API](references/policies.md#data-operations), enter representative visitor accounts and check the requested business journeys. Verify that each role sees its intended pages, that reset is repeatable and, when writes are enabled, that reset removes visitor additions. Report the application URL, visitor entry, demonstrated interactions, cleanup scope and checks performed.

For a CLI-only dataset, omit the page and visitor steps. A non-AI demo needs no model or Agent integration. With the application's jobs service composed, daily reset is always enabled after the first generation and reads its schedule from the deployment environment; see [reset variables and defaults](references/policies.md#daily-reset). Preserve other saved policies.

## Maintain an application that uses Demo Mode

An application that registers a demo dataset keeps it in step with ordinary feature work. When a change adds or alters any of these, update the demo side in the same change:

- **Business collections or relations.** Extend the dataset's `clear(context)` to remove the new rows, dependent records first, and generate records where the demonstrated journeys need them; see [business cleanup](references/adapting-data.md#business-cleanup).
- **Outbound calls, file storage or notifications.** Route them through a demo fixture or refusal at the application boundary; see [external effects](references/integration-checklist.md#external-effects).
- **Background jobs, queues or schedules.** Decide whether each runs against fixtures or is disabled in the demo, and keep it from recreating cleared records; see [background work](references/integration-checklist.md#background-work).
- **Visitor mutations.** Add the collections the mutation writes to the [collection write exceptions](references/policies.md#collection-write-exceptions) only when the demo should allow it.

Then reset the demo and verify that no business rows from before the reset remain. Changes that touch none of these need no demo work.

## Required host capabilities

| Capability                    | Host registrations                                                                 |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Dataset CLI without accounts  | Database, Demo Mode Server/configuration and CLI                                   |
| Visitor accounts              | Users and Authentication; Authorization for Permission Sets and role scopes        |
| Quick sign-in                 | Authentication and Demo Mode Client; Authorization for automatic Super Admin entry |
| Management APIs/page          | Authentication and Authorization; Demo Mode Client for UI/locales                  |
| Automatic daily reset         | The application's jobs service (`JobExecutorServiceProvider`)                      |
| Simulated model / online chat | Optional Agents 1.0 with `agents.models.services`                                  |

## Confirm the dedicated deployment

Clear and reset delete all business data in the connected database, including visitor additions. Before enabling, confirm that every connection under `database.connections`, the storage directory (`APP_STORAGE_DIR`) and any shared service the configuration names belong only to this demo deployment, through its own environment file or deployment configuration. Never enable Demo Mode against a database holding production or development data. If the target cannot be confirmed from the user's stated deployment, ask before enabling.

Give the demo its own storage and databases:

- **Local trial.** Stop the normal development server and start a separate instance, such as `APP_STORAGE_DIR=storage/demo NOCOBASE_DEMO_MODE=true pnpm dev`. A relative SQLite filename, the template default, resolves under the storage directory, so this one variable separates both the database and the files. When the local environment uses a server database (`DB_DIALECT` other than `sqlite`), also set `DB_DATABASE` to a separate, empty database; `APP_STORAGE_DIR` alone would still reach the development database. The normal database is untouched.
- **Server deployment.** Use the deployment's own environment file or `config.yml` with a distinct `APP_STORAGE_DIR` and distinct connection values: `DB_DATABASE` (with its host and credentials) for a server database, or `DB_FILENAME` for an absolute SQLite path. Give every additional connection its own database too.

`APP_STORAGE_DIR` also separates the template's default memory queue and jobs state and its local `fs` disk, but not external services. Check the configuration of both instances, including a local trial beside the development server:

- **Redis.** When `queue.default`, `jobs.default`, the session store or a caching provider uses Redis, give the demo its own Redis instance or a distinct `db` number in each of those sections. A shared Redis lets one instance consume the other's queue messages and job firings and write them into its own database.
- **File disks.** When `drive.default` or a disk the application uses is `s3` or another remote driver, give the demo its own bucket or prefix. Cleanup of generated and visitor-uploaded files acts on that disk.

A new demo database starts with only the initial administrator, created on first start from `INITIAL_ADMIN_USERNAME`, `INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD` (`users.initialAdmin`); without them it is `nocobase` / `admin@nocobase.com` / `admin123`. This administrator holds the unrestricted root Permission Set, so it can open the read-only management page and use the data API without extra grants. In Demo Mode this account is publicly enterable alongside other enabled person accounts. Anonymous visitors opening the home page or a protected application route enter it automatically; existing sessions are retained. No dataset generation is needed for this entry.

## Enable the deployment

Complete these steps in order, preserving existing registrations and configuration sections:

1. **Install and register.** Run `pnpm nocobase plugin register demo-mode --dry-run`, review the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`. While the package is not installed yet, the dry run only prints the install command and asks to run `register` again; that is expected, so run it without `--dry-run`, which installs and then registers. It adds the dependency, registers the Server, Client and CLI entries and synchronizes this Skill. Do not edit only one of `server/plugins.ts`, `client/plugins.ts` or `cli/plugins.ts` by hand. Keep the Client registration as `demoMode()` and add the [required header entry](references/visitor-entry.md#required-header-entry) in the application's layout.
2. **Register the configuration section.** Without it, neither `NOCOBASE_DEMO_MODE` nor a `demoMode` section is read. Follow the application's one-file-per-section layout: create `server/config/demo-mode.ts`,

   ```ts
   import type { AppConfigFactory } from '@nocobase/app-server/config';
   import {
     defineDemoModeConfig,
     type DemoModeConfig,
   } from '@nocobase/app-plugin-demo-mode/config';

   const demoMode: AppConfigFactory<DemoModeConfig> = defineDemoModeConfig();

   export default demoMode;
   ```

   then add it to `server/config/index.ts` in both places the other sections appear, keeping the existing entries:

   ```ts
   import demoMode from './demo-mode.js';

   const defaultConfigs: AppConfigFactory<{
     // ...existing sections
     demoMode: ReturnType<typeof demoMode>;
   }> = defaultAppConfigs({
     // ...existing sections
     demoMode,
   });
   ```

3. **Switch it on.** Set `NOCOBASE_DEMO_MODE=true` in this deployment's environment (its process environment or environment file), or set it in this deployment's `config.yml`:

   ```yaml
   demoMode:
     enabled: true
   ```

   Run `pnpm nocobase config check`, then start or restart. Startup applies the plugin's migrations while `migrations.autoRun` is `true`, the template default; otherwise run `pnpm nocobase db apply` first.

4. **Verify.**
   - `GET <base path>/api/demoMode/status` returns `{ "data": { "enabled": true } }`, and the startup log contains `Demo mode is on`. `false` with the variable set means the configuration section is not registered.
   - Signed in as an administrator, an ordinary change outside the [write exceptions](references/policies.md#collection-write-exceptions), such as editing a business record or a user profile, fails with 400 and `error.reason: DEMO_READ_ONLY`.
   - Startup refuses to continue when a database connection cannot be guarded; see [troubleshooting](references/minimal-example.md#troubleshooting).
   - When Agents is registered, its chat and Agent runs are not covered by the write guard. Demo Mode then creates an enabled simulated model service, `Demo chat`, but does not redirect Agents to it: Agents uses its saved default chat model, or else the first enabled chat model service. In a new demo database that is `Demo chat`. Check the model services in the demo database: keep no real provider credentials there, leave no real service saved as the default or enabled ahead of `Demo chat`, and either integrate [simulation](references/simulation.md) or confirm that chat is unavailable to visitors.

Use the plugin defaults for quick sign-in and scheduling. Customize only what the requested demo needs. Demo Mode is disabled by default in ordinary deployments.

## Management access

While Demo Mode is enabled, root, including the initial administrator, is unrestricted and can open the management page without grants. Give page viewers `settings:demoMode.data` `read` and `settings:demoMode.configuration` `read`. The page is read-only for every account, including root: it shows status, the reset schedule and account entry links, with no data operations or language selector. Grant `settings:demoMode.data` `manage` or `settings:demoMode.configuration` `configure` only for the corresponding API mutations. A dataset account may hold these actions too when the demo should show administration, through the dataset's `createPermissionSet`; reset restores whatever a visitor changes. Clear and failed reset automatically preserve the executing administrator's existing access; see [administrator lifecycle](references/adapting-data.md#keep-the-executing-administrator-available).

These settings items are registered only while Demo Mode is enabled. In an ordinary deployment of the same application, `authz.settings.grant('demoMode.data', …)` throws `Unknown settings item`, and `demoModeRoutes()` omits the management menu and route. Do not add these grants to seeds or migrations that also run in ordinary deployments: assign them in the demo deployment through permission administration, through the dataset's Permission Sets, or from code that runs only when `demoModeServiceToken` reports `enabled`.

| Run a new non-AI demo with schema, API and pages   | [Minimal application example](references/minimal-example.md) |

| Operate data or customize write/reset policies     | [Operations and policies](references/policies.md)            |

# Demo Mode

Use `@nocobase/app-plugin-demo-mode` for a dedicated demo with its own database and storage. The plugin supplies data lifecycle, visitor accounts, write protection, management components and optional simulation. The application supplies its business records, cleanup and external adapters. Simulation adapters and demo chat are enabled by default once integrated, without AI switches on the management page; the application chooses which flows to connect.

## Check that this Skill applies

Demo Mode refuses ordinary writes, resets data daily and deletes all business data on clear/reset. Apply it only when the user asks for a demo deployment with those properties, names this plugin or Demo Mode, or the application already depends on it. Otherwise use the matching workflow:

| Request                                                                                | Use instead                                                        |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Example or sample records, such as “add some demo customers”                           | The application development Skill's sample-data workflow           |
| A trial, staging, test or customer environment where users keep their own data         | The `nocobase-deployment` Skill; an ordinary deployment without it |
| A payment, mail or other provider's sandbox account or test credentials                | That integration's configuration                                   |
| An in-app “demo/presentation mode” feature, such as hiding fields while screen-sharing | Ordinary feature development                                       |

When the request could mean either a Demo Mode deployment or one of these, ask which one the user wants before registering the plugin, enabling it or adding full-business cleanup. For a confirmed dedicated demo, reuse the user's established deployment, language and role choices, and clarify any unresolved deployment or cleanup scope: clear/reset removes all business data in the demo instance, including visitor additions.

## Keep protection proportionate

A demo is a public showcase: anyone may enter any listed account, administrators included, and the fictional data is reset daily. Protect only what lies outside the demo: a dedicated database and storage, no real credentials or customer data, and no real external effects such as mail, payments, publishing or real models. Inside the demo, use the application's existing permissions as they are and the plugin's defaults. Do not add hardening such as ownership rechecks, rate limits, confirmation steps, management restrictions for dataset accounts or security-focused tests unless the user asks; prefer the simplest integration that shows the requested journeys.

## Integration workflow

1. **Confirm the target and enable.** Check [the dedicated deployment](#confirm-the-dedicated-deployment), then complete [enable the deployment](#enable-the-deployment) and its verification. Check the required host capabilities below.
2. **Provide the dataset.** Adapt the application's business services using [data adaptation](references/adapting-data.md). For a new application with no business domain, use the [executable non-AI example](references/minimal-example.md). Register one dataset on the original `demoDataToken` in an application provider's `boot()`; registration does not generate records.
3. **Adapt interactions.** Keep normal business authorization. Enable [collection write exceptions](references/policies.md#collection-write-exceptions) for visitor mutations. The guard covers request-scoped database writes; adapt [external calls and background work](references/integration-checklist.md) where the application has them. Read [simulation](references/simulation.md) only for AI or Runner flows the demo uses.
4. **Provide entry and management.** Mount `DemoModeSettings` from `@nocobase/app-plugin-demo-mode/client/settings` on an application-owned page inside the application's existing System management (settings) navigation group, protected by `settings:demoMode.data/read`. Wrap its route declarations with `demoModeRoutes([...])` from `@nocobase/app-plugin-demo-mode/client` so both the menu and route are absent outside Demo Mode, including for root. `defineDemoModeConfig()` publishes the enabled flag automatically; existing applications must adopt the helper. Grant [management access](#management-access) and see the [route example](references/minimal-example.md#2-wire-existing-composition-roots). Visitor accounts keep their business permissions. The Client plugin automatically enters Super Admin for anonymous visitors opening the home page or a protected application route and provides `/demo-sign-in` for all enabled person accounts; mount the standalone `DemoModeMenu` in the top header actions as described in [visitor entry](references/visitor-entry.md#required-header-entry).
5. **Generate and verify.** Generate through the [CLI or API](references/policies.md#data-operations), enter representative visitor accounts and check the requested business journeys. Verify that each role sees its intended pages, that reset is repeatable and, when writes are enabled, that reset removes visitor additions. Report the application URL, visitor entry, demonstrated interactions, cleanup scope and checks performed.

For a CLI-only dataset, omit the page and visitor steps. A non-AI demo needs no model or Agent integration. With the application's jobs service composed, daily reset is always enabled after the first generation and reads its schedule from the deployment environment; see [reset variables and defaults](references/policies.md#daily-reset). Preserve other saved policies.

An application that registers a demo dataset keeps it in step with ordinary feature work. When a change adds or alters any of these, update the demo side in the same change:

- **Outbound calls, file storage or notifications.** Route them through a demo fixture or refusal at the application boundary; see [external effects](references/integration-checklist.md#external-effects).
- **Background jobs, queues or schedules.** Decide whether each runs against fixtures or is disabled in the demo, and keep it from recreating cleared records; see [background work](references/integration-checklist.md#background-work).

| Capability                    | Host registrations                                                                 |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Dataset CLI without accounts  | Database, Demo Mode Server/configuration and CLI                                   |
| Visitor accounts              | Users and Authentication; Authorization for Permission Sets and role scopes        |
| Quick sign-in                 | Authentication and Demo Mode Client; Authorization for automatic Super Admin entry |
| Management APIs/page          | Authentication and Authorization; Demo Mode Client for UI/locales                  |
| Automatic daily reset         | The application's jobs service (`JobExecutorServiceProvider`)                      |
| Simulated model / online chat | Optional Agents 1.0 with `agents.models.services`                                  |

## Confirm the dedicated deployment

Clear and reset delete all business data in the connected database, including visitor additions. Before enabling, confirm that every connection under `database.connections`, the storage directory (`APP_STORAGE_DIR`) and any shared service the configuration names belong only to this demo deployment, through its own environment file or deployment configuration. Never enable Demo Mode against a database holding production or development data. If the target cannot be confirmed from the user's stated deployment, ask before enabling.

Give the demo its own storage and databases:

- **Local trial.** Stop the normal development server and start a separate instance, such as `APP_STORAGE_DIR=storage/demo NOCOBASE_DEMO_MODE=true pnpm dev`. A relative SQLite filename, the template default, resolves under the storage directory, so this one variable separates both the database and the files. When the local environment uses a server database (`DB_DIALECT` other than `sqlite`), also set `DB_DATABASE` to a separate, empty database; `APP_STORAGE_DIR` alone would still reach the development database. The normal database is untouched.
- **Server deployment.** Use the deployment's own environment file or `config.yml` with a distinct `APP_STORAGE_DIR` and distinct connection values: `DB_DATABASE` (with its host and credentials) for a server database, or `DB_FILENAME` for an absolute SQLite path. Give every additional connection its own database too.

`APP_STORAGE_DIR` also separates the template's default memory queue and jobs state and its local `fs` disk, but not external services. Check the configuration of both instances, including a local trial beside the development server:

- **Redis.** When `queue.default`, `jobs.default`, the session store or a caching provider uses Redis, give the demo its own Redis instance or a distinct `db` number in each of those sections. A shared Redis lets one instance consume the other's queue messages and job firings and write them into its own database.
- **File disks.** When `drive.default` or a disk the application uses is `s3` or another remote driver, give the demo its own bucket or prefix. Cleanup of generated and visitor-uploaded files acts on that disk.

A new demo database starts with only the initial administrator, created on first start from `INITIAL_ADMIN_USERNAME`, `INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD` (`users.initialAdmin`); without them it is `nocobase` / `admin@nocobase.com` / `admin123`. Complete these steps in order, preserving existing registrations and configuration sections:

1. **Install and register.** Run `pnpm nocobase plugin register demo-mode --dry-run`, review the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`. While the package is not installed yet, the dry run only prints the install command and asks to run `register` again; that is expected, so run it without `--dry-run`, which installs and then registers. It adds the dependency, registers the Server, Client and CLI entries and synchronizes this Skill. Do not edit only one of `server/plugins.ts`, `client/plugins.ts` or `cli/plugins.ts` by hand.    ```ts

   ```ts
     defineDemoModeConfig,
     type DemoModeConfig,
   } from '@nocobase/app-plugin-demo-mode/config';

   ```

   ```ts
   import demoMode from './demo-mode.js';

     // ...existing sections
     demoMode: ReturnType<typeof demoMode>;
   }> = defaultAppConfigs({
     // ...existing sections
     demoMode,
   ```

   Run `pnpm nocobase config check`, then start or restart. Startup applies the plugin's migrations while `migrations.autoRun` is `true`, the template default; otherwise run `pnpm nocobase db apply` first.

   - When Agents is registered, its chat and Agent runs are not covered by the write guard. Demo Mode then creates an enabled simulated model service, `Demo chat`, but does not redirect Agents to it: Agents uses its saved default chat model, or else the first enabled chat model service. In a new demo database that is `Demo chat`. Check the model services in the demo database: keep no real provider credentials there, leave no real service saved as the default or enabled ahead of `Demo chat`, and either integrate [simulation](references/simulation.md) or confirm that chat is unavailable to visitors.

Clear and failed reset automatically preserve the executing administrator's existing access; see [administrator lifecycle](references/adapting-data.md#keep-the-executing-administrator-available).

These settings items are registered only while Demo Mode is enabled. In an ordinary deployment of the same application, `authz.settings.grant('demoMode.data', …)` throws `Unknown settings item`, and `demoModeRoutes()` omits the management menu and route. Do not add these grants to seeds or migrations that also run in ordinary deployments: assign them in the demo deployment through permission administration, through the dataset's Permission Sets, or from code that runs only when `demoModeServiceToken` reports `enabled`.

skills.body:
---
name: nocobase-app-plugin-distributed
description: Configure or diagnose multi-instance NocoBase 3 applications, including shared Redis caching, concurrency, Jobs, Queue and Realtime. Use for horizontal scaling, cross-instance coordination and distributed backend rollout. Not for creating an application, implementing Redis adapters, or deploying a single-instance application without a scaling requirement.
---

# Distributed applications

This package provides guidance only. It has no runtime exports, configuration section, UI or automatically registered adapters. Do not add a `distributed` section to `config.yml` or register this package in a runtime plugin list. A synchronized Skill is not evidence that an application is distributed.

## Inspect the application first

Read the application's `AGENTS.md`, installed deployment Skill and the compatible Skills for the services being changed. Inspect `package.json`, the lockfile, `server/plugins.ts`, configuration factories, `config.yml`, environment mappings, file storage and deployment topology. Use the installed versions' public declarations and documentation; a source checkout is not required.

Record each service's effective selector, adapter, shared destination, namespace and overrides without exposing credentials. Distinguish a dependency being installed, a Server plugin being registered, a backend being selected, and successful cross-instance verification. Inspect named backends selected by business code as well as the default. Do not assume every application needs every Redis plugin.

## Configure and verify

1. Establish the intended instance count, public origin and shared infrastructure. Inventory existing persistent data, active jobs, queues and file storage before planning a switch. Follow [shared infrastructure and rollout](references/rollout.md).
2. Map each required service to its configuration and implementation using [backend configuration](references/backends.md). Keep unused services unchanged and preserve application-owned custom providers.
3. Resolve compatible runtime packages and commercial access before selecting their adapters. Use the target application's commercial-package access instructions and existing credentials. If unavailable, distinguish access denial, missing version and network failure, report the gap and continue independent preparation. Never substitute memory and call the application distributed.
4. Install required packages and explicitly register their supported Server exports. Read each package's own Skill and typed configuration before editing its settings. Merge changes into existing application configuration; do not replace unrelated sections or expose connection credentials in browser configuration.
5. Run the application's configuration validation, scoped checks and build. Configuration validation alone does not prove connectivity, plugin activation or distributed behavior. Start an isolated two-instance verification using shared infrastructure and verify the relevant operations in [the rollout checklist](references/rollout.md).
6. Report what changed, effective service selections, verification evidence and remaining blockers. Scale production only within the user's authorization, after the applicable verification succeeds.

## Ownership and limits

The application owns its configuration, Server composition, business operations, deployment manifests and access rules. Each runtime plugin owns its public adapters and connection lifecycle. This plugin owns only this Skill and its references. Edit these sources when maintaining the plugin, never the application's generated Skill copies.

Use original service Tokens and registered public APIs. Distributed coordination does not expand user permissions, make application side effects exactly-once, migrate in-memory work to Redis, or make local files shared. Read the owning plugin's supported topology and failure semantics; do not promise Cluster or Sentinel support without version-specific evidence.

skills.name: nocobase-app-plugin-foundation
skills.desc: Use when an application should show its administrators which NocoBase Core capabilities it uses (the App Foundation page), when registering or moving that page, or when asked why a capability shows as in use, needing setup, not used or undetermined there. skills.body:
---
name: nocobase-app-plugin-foundation
description: Use when an application should show its administrators which NocoBase Core capabilities it uses (the App Foundation page), when registering or moving that page, or when asked why a capability shows as in use, needing setup, not used or undetermined there. Not for business permissions or for building other admin pages.
---

# App Foundation

## Use this Skill when

- The application should get the App Foundation page, or it should move or leave the menu.
- Someone asks why a capability on that page is in use, needs setup, is not used yet or is undetermined, or where a number comes from.

The App Foundation runtime page admits only unrestricted access by design. The separate Features and extensions catalog and its detail pages require `page:capability-guide/access` (`CAPABILITY_GUIDE_ACCESS` from the client entry). That grant may be assigned through permission sets; it does not grant access to Foundation runtime information or to the management APIs linked by the catalog.

## Public surfaces

- Server plugin: `@nocobase/app-plugin-foundation/server` (default export). Exports `foundationServiceToken`, whose `snapshot()`, `scanStatus()` and `ensureScan({ refresh?, countRecords? })` read saved data and submit background scans. Compatibility `overview()` reads a saved overview or reports `FOUNDATION_PENDING`.
- Configuration: `@nocobase/app-plugin-foundation/config` exports `defineFoundationConfig()` and `FoundationConfig` for the application's `foundation` section, whose only setting is `scanOnStart` (default `true`, environment `FOUNDATION_SCAN_ON_START`).
- Server route: `GET /api/foundation/overview` returns durable scan state and an optional `overview`. Use `POST /api/foundation/ensureScan`, `/refresh` or `/countRecords` to submit work; GET mutation flags are rejected. Ordinary loads and refreshes do not count every business table. Requires a session or API key of an identity with unrestricted access; anyone else gets `403` with reason `FOUNDATION_FORBIDDEN`.
- Collection list: `GET /api/foundation/collections?offset=0&search=orders`, the same unrestricted access boundary, at most 50 entries in `{ data, meta: { total } }`. Search covers the full owned catalog, not just the displayed page.
- Client plugin: `@nocobase/app-plugin-foundation/client` (default export). `foundation()` adds the page at `/foundation` with a menu entry; options `path`, `navigation: false`, `routes: false` and `settingsGroup: true`. The default template uses `settingsGroup: true` so a bare application already has a localized settings group containing only the protected Foundation page.
- Page component: `FoundationPage` from `@nocobase/app-plugin-foundation/client/pages`, for an application that routes it itself (`foundation({ routes: false })`). Declare such a route with `authz: 'unrestricted'`.

## Prerequisites

The authentication and authorization plugins are registered, as in the default template. The page reads the query cache the application's routes provide.

## App workflow

1. Add the dependency and register the server plugin in `server/plugins.ts` and the client plugin in `client/plugins.ts`.
2. Restart the application and open `/foundation` as an administrator holding the root Permission Set.
3. Build the application as usual; refresh the page to see new capabilities light up.

## Reading a status

- Collected read-only by the plugin; nothing reports to it, so there is nothing to register per capability.
- In use means wired in: a persisted lifecycle, an enabled schedule, a connected mailbox, a configured notification channel, an API key that has been used. Zero uses still count as in use.
- Needs setup names what is missing in its reason, such as `noChannel` or `noDrive`.
- Information pending update means the evidence could not be read this time, never that it is unused. Use the top Refresh button to collect again; capability details have no separate retry button. If the initial page request fails with no overview or top Refresh available, use the page's Try again button. Expand the read details for sanitized source notes. Permission denial still hides cached information and offers no retry.
- AI and agents are in use with an enabled model service or a registered Runner. Native OnlineAgent and model gateway calls do not require an `agAgents` record. Stored Agent definitions and historical usage alone do not prove current configuration. Keep unreadable execution paths as pending subparts so reliable active evidence and metrics can retain their original dates. A successfully read zero invalidates that path's earlier active evidence through subsequent failures. If neither execution path has current or retained active evidence and a required read failed, leave the status undetermined. Preserve another confirmed active path when optional statistics fail; never turn a failed read into zero or a missing-configuration claim.
- Observed table scope uses `server/catalog.ts`. Known system Collections are excluded. Remaining tables are observed data without proven business ownership; unknown extensions never suppress their statistics or generate a read failure. Show identified/counting results and keep the ownership boundary in expandable recognition notes.

## Verification

The application service keeps reliable active statuses, subpart statuses and complete metrics in the saved checkpoint. Retained values expose their original `checkedAt` and display “Last confirmed”; the overview timestamp is the latest check. Current reliable values take precedence, including zero. Earlier unused or needs-setup states do not become current negative conclusions after a failure. File counts, bytes and table counts require complete candidate discovery as well as successful aggregation to be exact. Without complete history, partial values carry an explicit lower-bound explanation; wholly unreadable values remain pending. A fully confirmed empty catalog still reports exact zero. File facts retained from complete discovery carry their original date as well.

Snapshots and reliable history persist in the private `foundationSnapshots` Collection, isolated by application and default connection. A scan starts only on first use, running NocoBase server kernel version changes or an explicit POST. `foundation.scanOnStart` (`FOUNDATION_SCAN_ON_START`, factory `defineFoundationConfig()` from `@nocobase/app-plugin-foundation/config`) defaults to `true`; `false` submits nothing at application start, so closing the application waits for no scan, while page visits, Refresh, Count records and an already claimed generation still run. `@nocobase/app-testing` test applications default to `false`; pass `config: { foundation: { scanOnStart: true } }` to a test that needs the start-up scan. Structural/configuration changes and business writes never trigger scans. Same-kernel restarts read saved data. Jobs executes a generation claimed and published through Repository optimistic locking. Memory Jobs recovers unfinished state at startup in one process; multiple processes use the host’s Redis Jobs. Failed attempts preserve the prior completion time and require manual retry. Active pages poll small status columns every two seconds and read the snapshot once on completion; idle pages do not poll. Authorization precedes every route, and `401` or `403` hides cached internals.

The existing deadline preserves evidence completed before another read stalled, including confirmed configuration and partial file statistics. This does not issue a second query or extend the deadline. Late completions cannot replace the response, and queries already in flight retain their shared slots until they settle.

- As the root administrator, `/foundation` shows the capabilities available in this runtime, and `GET /api/foundation/overview` answers `200`.
- As any other user, the page is not in the menu, and the route answers `403 FOUNDATION_FORBIDDEN`.
- After adding a Collection, a lifecycle or a notification channel and refreshing, the matching capability changes.

## Reading the provider inventory

The visible capability band is dynamic, not a fixed thirteen-item catalog. The optional overview `inventory` lists package manifests, catalog category associations and observed current registration separately. The browser adds Client route and provider owners as view-only evidence. # App Foundation

## Use this Skill when

- The application should get the App Foundation page, or it should move or leave the menu.
- Someone asks why a capability on that page is in use, needs setup, is not used yet or is undetermined, or where a number comes from.

The App Foundation runtime page admits only unrestricted access by design. The separate Features and extensions catalog and its detail pages require `page:capability-guide/access` (`CAPABILITY_GUIDE_ACCESS` from the client entry). That grant may be assigned through permission sets; it does not grant access to Foundation runtime information or to the management APIs linked by the catalog.

## Public surfaces

- Server plugin: `@nocobase/app-plugin-foundation/server` (default export). Exports `foundationServiceToken`, whose `snapshot()`, `scanStatus()` and `ensureScan({ refresh?, countRecords? })` read saved data and submit background scans. Compatibility `overview()` reads a saved overview or reports `FOUNDATION_PENDING`.
- Configuration: `@nocobase/app-plugin-foundation/config` exports `defineFoundationConfig()` and `FoundationConfig` for the application's `foundation` section, whose only setting is `scanOnStart` (default `true`, environment `FOUNDATION_SCAN_ON_START`).
- Server route: `GET /api/foundation/overview` returns durable scan state and an optional `overview`. Use `POST /api/foundation/ensureScan`, `/refresh` or `/countRecords` to submit work; GET mutation flags are rejected. Ordinary loads and refreshes do not count every business table. Requires a session or API key of an identity with unrestricted access; anyone else gets `403` with reason `FOUNDATION_FORBIDDEN`.
- Collection list: `GET /api/foundation/collections?offset=0&search=orders`, the same unrestricted access boundary, at most 50 entries in `{ data, meta: { total } }`. Search covers the full owned catalog, not just the displayed page.
- Client plugin: `@nocobase/app-plugin-foundation/client` (default export). `foundation()` adds the page at `/foundation` with a menu entry; options `path`, `navigation: false`, `routes: false` and `settingsGroup: true`. The default template uses `settingsGroup: true` so a bare application already has a localized settings group containing only the protected Foundation page.
- Page component: `FoundationPage` from `@nocobase/app-plugin-foundation/client/pages`, for an application that routes it itself (`foundation({ routes: false })`). Declare such a route with `authz: 'unrestricted'`.

## Prerequisites

The authentication and authorization plugins are registered, as in the default template. The page reads the query cache the application's routes provide.

## App workflow

1. Add the dependency and register the server plugin in `server/plugins.ts` and the client plugin in `client/plugins.ts`.
2. Restart the application and open `/foundation` as an administrator holding the root Permission Set.
3. Build the application as usual; refresh the page to see new capabilities light up.

## Reading a status

- Collected read-only by the plugin; nothing reports to it, so there is nothing to register per capability.
- In use means wired in: a persisted lifecycle, an enabled schedule, a connected mailbox, a configured notification channel, an API key that has been used. Zero uses still count as in use.
- Needs setup names what is missing in its reason, such as `noChannel` or `noDrive`.
- Information pending update means the evidence could not be read this time, never that it is unused. Use the top Refresh button to collect again; capability details have no separate retry button. If the initial page request fails with no overview or top Refresh available, use the page's Try again button. Expand the read details for sanitized source notes. Permission denial still hides cached information and offers no retry.
- AI and agents are in use with an enabled model service or a registered Runner. Native OnlineAgent and model gateway calls do not require an `agAgents` record. Stored Agent definitions and historical usage alone do not prove current configuration. Keep unreadable execution paths as pending subparts so reliable active evidence and metrics can retain their original dates. A successfully read zero invalidates that path's earlier active evidence through subsequent failures. If neither execution path has current or retained active evidence and a required read failed, leave the status undetermined. Preserve another confirmed active path when optional statistics fail; never turn a failed read into zero or a missing-configuration claim.
- Observed table scope uses `server/catalog.ts`. Known system Collections are excluded. Remaining tables are observed data without proven business ownership; unknown extensions never suppress their statistics or generate a read failure. Show identified/counting results and keep the ownership boundary in expandable recognition notes.

Retained values expose their original `checkedAt` and display “Last confirmed”; the overview timestamp is the latest check. Current reliable values take precedence, including zero. Earlier unused or needs-setup states do not become current negative conclusions after a failure. File counts, bytes and table counts require complete candidate discovery as well as successful aggregation to be exact. Without complete history, partial values carry an explicit lower-bound explanation; wholly unreadable values remain pending. A fully confirmed empty catalog still reports exact zero. File facts retained from complete discovery carry their original date as well.

Snapshots and reliable history persist in the private `foundationSnapshots` Collection, isolated by application and default connection. A scan starts only on first use, running NocoBase server kernel version changes or an explicit POST. `foundation.scanOnStart` (`FOUNDATION_SCAN_ON_START`, factory `defineFoundationConfig()` from `@nocobase/app-plugin-foundation/config`) defaults to `true`; `false` submits nothing at application start, so closing the application waits for no scan, while page visits, Refresh, Count records and an already claimed generation still run. `@nocobase/app-testing` test applications default to `false`; pass `config: { foundation: { scanOnStart: true } }` to a test that needs the start-up scan.
